name: Kerala and the Tamil temple country: Kochi, Kuttanad, Munnar

cities.base: Fort Kochi, on the streets between the beachfront and Santa Cruz Basilica, or Mattancherry if you want the working town rather than the heritage one. You walk everywhere in Fort Kochi, the Mattancherr
cities.name: Kochi: Fort Kochi and Mattancherry

cities.base: Not Alappuzha town, which is traffic and a bus stand. Stay in a canal-side homestay or heritage house on the north canal or out at Punnamada, or better, 20 minutes south at Nedumudy or Chennamkary in
cities.name: Alappuzha and the Kuttanad backwaters

cities.base: Avoid Munnar town itself, which is a bazaar, a bus stand and a traffic jam with hotels. Stay in the estates 5 to 12 km out on the Chithirapuram, Pothamedu or Bison Valley side, where you step out of t
cities.name: Munnar and the Kannan Devan tea hills

cities.base: You do not sleep up here. Rajamalai is 13 km from Munnar, Kolukkumalai is a 4WD hour beyond Suryanelli, Marayoor and Chinnar are 40 to 60 km north on the Udumalpet road. All of it runs off a Munnar be
cities.name: The high range: Rajamalai, Kolukkumalai and Marayoor

cities.base: Inside the Masi streets, the concentric ring roads around the temple, so you can walk to the East gate at 05:30 and back at 22:00 after the night procession. North Masi and the Town Hall Road side hav
cities.name: Madurai

cities.base: Thanjavur near the palace and East Main Street, ten minutes by auto from the Big Temple and central for the Kumbakonam and Trichy loops. Kumbakonam is the alternative and puts you next to Darasuram an
cities.name: Thanjavur and the Chola country

places.name: The Chinese fishing nets, Vasco da Gama Square
places.note: Cantilevered dip nets, about a dozen of them, and maybe half still fish; the crews will wave you onto the platform and then ask 200 to 500 rupees for the privilege of hauling the rope. The fish stalls behind them, where you buy a kingfish and pay a second shack to fry it, are the oldest overcharge i

places.name: St Francis Church
places.note: Built by the Portuguese around 1503 and the oldest European church in India; Vasco da Gama was buried under the floor here in 1524 and the empty slab is still marked. It is a working CSI congregation, so Sunday morning until about 10:30 is a service and not a visit.

places.name: Mattancherry Palace, the Dutch Palace
places.note: Closed Fridays, and the ticket is a few rupees, so the only cost is getting there. Built by the Portuguese, renovated by the Dutch, and the reason to go is the bedchamber murals: dense sixteenth and seventeenth century Kerala painting of the Ramayana with no free wall left. No photography inside, en

places.name: Paradesi Synagogue
places.note: Shut Fridays and Saturdays and on Jewish holidays, and it breaks for lunch roughly 12:00 to 15:00, so the real window is two short slots. Built 1568, floored in hand painted Cantonese tiles no two of which match, and the congregation is now down to a handful of people. Shoes off, no cameras, and twe

places.name: Bazaar Road and the Jew Town spice godowns
places.note: The working end of Mattancherry: open warehouse doors with sacks of ginger, black pepper, turmeric and copra, men weighing by hand, and the smell changing every thirty metres. Most godowns are shut Sunday and half shut by 17:00. The antique shops at the Jew Town end are dearer than Delhi and much of

places.name: Kerala Kathakali Centre
places.note: Makeup from 17:00 and the performance 18:00 to 19:00 for about 600 rupees; arrive for the makeup or do not bother, because watching the green paste go on is half of it. This is a one hour tourist cutdown of a form that runs all night; real temple Kathakali happens December to April at temple festiva

places.name: Kayees Rahmathulla Cafe
places.note: Open since 1948 and the mutton biryani that Kochi argues about; short grain kaima rice, a boiled egg, and it is gone when it is gone, usually inside two hours of opening. Evening hours exist but the biryani is a lunch thing. Cash, shared tables, ten minutes walk from the synagogue. I am not certain

places.name: A banana leaf sadya, Ernakulam side
places.note: The full vegetarian sadya is a lunch-only event at ordinary meals hotels: twenty odd items round a leaf, rice in the middle, parippu then sambar then rasam then buttermilk in that order, payasam at the end. Eat right hand only, fold the leaf towards you when done. On Onam in late August or early Sep
places.neighborhood: MG Road and Warriam Road, Ernakulam

places.name: Kashi Art Cafe
places.note: The Fort Kochi cafe that started the whole Fort Kochi cafe thing, in a Dutch house with a courtyard and a small gallery at the back. Good filter coffee and a decent breakfast, priced for foreigners, full of them. Fine for a slow first morning, not a discovery.

places.name: Fusion Bay
places.note: Small, plain, family run, and the karimeen pollichathu and the prawn moilee are better than anything on the seafront strip at half the price. They will show you the day's fish. Ask for the Syrian Christian style fish curry with kudampuli, the sour smoked tamarind that makes Kerala fish curry taste l

places.name: Dhe Puttu
places.note: Puttu, the steamed rice and coconut cylinder that is the Kerala breakfast, served fifteen ways with beef, kadala curry and fish. A local-crowd restaurant rather than a heritage one, twenty five minutes by auto from Fort Kochi, and the single easiest place to understand why Kerala eats what it eats.

places.name: Kumbalangi and the toddy shops
places.note: A fishing and crab farming village on the backwater edge where the Chinese nets still work for a living and the coconut climbers still tap toddy. A kallu shaap is an unsigned concrete room with a bench, fresh toddy in a steel jug, and the hottest fish curry in Kerala; the toddy is sweet before noon
places.neighborhood: Kumbalangi, 15 km south of Fort Kochi

places.name: The overnight kettuvallam on Vembanad
places.note: Board around noon, cruise four hours, anchor by law before sunset, eat what the cook makes, sleep to a generator, move again at 07:00. Around 1,500 boats work this lake and the cheap ones at 6,000 rupees pump sewage and engine oil straight into water that villages still wash in. Pay 10,000 to 14,000

places.name: The Kuttanad village canoe out of Nedumudy
places.note: A punted country canoe down canals a houseboat cannot enter, past paddy fields farmed two metres below sea level behind mud bunds, duck herds, coir soaking in the water and toddy tappers overhead. This is the backwaters people actually mean. Book through a village homestay rather than a beach tout,

places.name: St Mary's Forane Church, Champakulam
places.note: A Syro-Malabar church the local tradition dates to AD 427, rebuilt many times, with a granite cross and Portuguese-era altarpieces inside. Kerala had Christians for a thousand years before any European arrived and this canal-side parish is the clearest place to feel that. Open to anyone, no fee, qui

places.name: Ambalappuzha Sree Krishna Temple
places.note: Famous for its palpayasam, a milk and rice pudding cooked since the sixteenth century, and non-Hindus are not admitted past the outer gate, which means you cannot see the temple or buy the payasam. Men who are admitted must go shirtless and women in a saree or mundu. Kerala is strict about this in a

places.name: Mullackal Street bazaar
places.note: Alappuzha's own shopping street: gold shops, banana chip fryers working in coconut oil in the open, coir, cloth, and tea stalls. Most of it shuts Sunday. The Rajarajeswari temple halfway along does not admit non-Hindus, but the street around it is the point.

places.name: A Kuttanad kallu shaap
places.note: Toddy shops are licensed, numbered and almost never named on a board, so you find them by asking, not by searching a map; your canoe punter or houseboat cook knows which one is pouring fresh today. What you go for is the food: karimeen fried in a banana leaf, duck roast, kappa and meen curry, clams,

places.name: Thaff Restaurant
places.note: Alappuzha's late night grill and biryani place, popular with locals rather than houseboat guests, and the kuzhi mandi and al faham show how much Gulf migration has rewritten Kerala's Muslim cooking. Loud, bright, fast. Good after a day on the water when everything else has closed.

places.name: Karimeen pollichathu on the Kumarakom road
places.note: Pearl spot fish, scored, packed with a chilli and shallot masala, wrapped in banana leaf and cooked on a tawa until the leaf chars. The small kitchens on the road in from Kottayam do it better and for a quarter of the price of the lakefront resorts. Almost all karimeen is now pond-farmed, which is w
places.neighborhood: Kumarakom lakefront, 30 km from Alappuzha by road

places.name: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
places.note: Fourteen acres of mangrove and rubber on the lake edge, walked on raised paths. Migrants including Siberian stork, teal and pintail are there November to February and that is when it is worth the drive; outside those months you get egrets, darters and cormorants and it is a nice wet walk, nothing mo

places.name: Pathiramanal island by shikara
places.note: A ten hectare island in the middle of the lake, reached by an hour of shikara, with a short birding trail and no shop and no shade to speak of. Take water. The trip is really about the crossing, which puts you out on open Vembanad away from the houseboat convoy, and about noticing how far the Thanne

places.name: Marari Beach
places.note: A long flat fishing beach with catamarans drawn up on it, a village behind and no promenade, which is the whole appeal after three days on brown water. The undertow is real and there are no lifeguards, so swim shallow. Sea jellies show up in some months and the fishermen will tell you which.

places.name: KDHP Tea Museum, Nallathanni Estate
places.note: Closed Mondays. A working demonstration of the rolling, oxidation and CTC line plus the original 1905 Pelton wheel, and the film on how Scots planters and Tamil labour built this district is honest about the labour part. The tasting at the end is short. Last entry is around 16:00 and it gets coach t
places.neighborhood: Nallathanni, 2 km north of Munnar town

places.name: The tea estate walk above Pothamedu
places.note: Estate roads and pluckers' paths through Kannan Devan tea, which is private land that nobody minds you walking on if you stay on the tracks and off the bushes. Go at 07:00 for the mist coming off the slopes and the pluckers going up with their shears. There is no marked route, so take a phone map an

places.name: Lockhart Gap
places.note: A road cut where the ridge drops into the Idukki valley and the cloud comes up through it in the afternoon. Free, no gate, no queue, and it is the one Munnar viewpoint that has not been fenced and ticketed. Best before 10:00 or you are looking at white.
places.neighborhood: On the Kochi road, 18 km south of Munnar

places.name: Mattupetty Dam and the Indo-Swiss dairy
places.note: A reservoir ringed by tea with a herd of crossbred cattle behind it, and the shore is genuinely good at eight in the morning. By eleven it is a car park, a row of corn roasters and men selling a twelve minute speedboat lap. Go early, keep walking past the boat jetty, and the crowd stops within two h

places.name: Echo Point
places.note: A lay-by where a coachload of people shout at a hillside and a smaller sound comes back. There is a ticket gate, a car park, pedal boats and a line of stalls. Drive through it to Top Station and spend the twenty minutes at Anayirankal instead.

places.name: Top Station
places.note: At 1,700 metres on the state line, looking down onto the Theni plains of Tamil Nadu, and it was the top of the old ropeway that took tea down to the plains before the road. Cloud usually fills the valley by 10:00, so this is a leave-at-06:30 trip or nothing. The Neelakurinji that people come for flo
places.neighborhood: Kerala and Tamil Nadu border, 32 km east of Munnar

places.name: Anayirankal reservoir
places.note: A bigger and much emptier reservoir than Mattupetty, ringed by tea and shola forest, with a dirt track along the shore you can walk for an hour. Elephants use the far bank and are occasionally on the near one at dusk, which is a reason to keep to the road and not camp. No gate and no fee.

places.name: CSI Christ Church, Munnar
places.note: A small granite church consecrated in 1910 for the planters, with their memorial brasses inside and a cemetery of people who died young of blackwater fever. Fifteen minutes, free, and it explains the town better than any viewpoint. Sunday morning is a service.

places.name: Munnar old bazaar
places.note: Two streets of spice shops, tea merchants selling by weight from open sacks, hardware and vegetable stalls. Buy tea loose here rather than in the tourist shops on the Aluva road, where the same leaf is in a tin at four times the price. Cardamom and pepper are genuinely worth carrying home; the tea d

places.name: The bazaar chaikada at four o'clock
places.note: A tea stall with a glass case of parippu vada and banana fritters, chai pulled between two steel tumblers to cool and froth it. Late afternoon is when the estate buses come down and the place fills with pluckers. Twenty rupees for tea and a vada, and it is the most Kerala thing in Munnar.

places.name: Rapsy Restaurant
places.note: A plain bazaar restaurant that has been feeding Munnar for decades and is now in every guidebook, which has cost it nothing. Kerala parotta with beef fry, kothu parotta, and a bhelpuri that has no business being in a hill town and is the thing people queue for. Cash, packed at 20:00, turnover fast.

places.name: The evening thattukada carts
places.note: Roadside carts that set up at dusk: kallappam, egg roast, beef ularthiyathu, omelette and porotta cooked on a kerosene griddle while you stand. This is where Kerala actually eats at night, it costs about 200 rupees, and it is the one place in Munnar with no foreigner pricing. Nothing is mild.
places.neighborhood: Munnar bridge and the Aluva road junction

places.name: Eravikulam National Park at Rajamalai
places.note: Closed completely from 1 February to 31 March every year for Nilgiri tahr calving, which no weekly closed-day field can express and which ruins a February itinerary built around it. Otherwise you book online, park at the gate, take the forest bus up and walk a 3 km tarred loop through shola grasslan
places.neighborhood: Rajamalai gate, 13 km north of Munnar

places.name: Kolukkumalai sunrise and the orthodox tea factory
places.note: Leave Munnar around 04:30, transfer to a 4WD jeep at Suryanelli, and take an hour of rock track that no car will do to a ridge at 2,100 metres for sunrise over the Tamil Nadu plains. The factory at the top still runs a 1930s orthodox line by belt drive and will show you the whole process. Jeeps are
places.neighborhood: Above Suryanelli, on the Tamil Nadu side

places.name: Lakkam Waterfalls
places.note: A forest department pool below a short fall, with changing rooms and a ticket gate, and it is a reasonable twenty minutes on the way to Marayoor. It is a trickle by March and closed outright when the river runs high in the monsoon. Do not make a special trip.
places.neighborhood: Marayoor road, 22 km north of Munnar

places.name: The Muniyara dolmens, Marayoor
places.note: Iron Age burial chambers, four granite slabs and a capstone each, scattered across fields and a low hill; some are 3,000 years old and there are hundreds in the valley. Barely signed, occasionally a caretaker with a key and a ticket book, mostly just there. The ones up the hill behind the school are

places.name: The Marayoor sandalwood forest
places.note: The only natural sandalwood stand in Kerala, state owned down to individual numbered trees because of a poaching history that involved Veerappan. You cannot walk in alone; the forest office at Marayoor runs escorted entry and the rules change, so this is a turn-up-and-ask rather than a booking. The

places.name: The Marayoor jaggery sheds
places.note: Marayoor sharkara has a geographical indication and is made in open sheds beside the cane fields: crushed juice boiled down in an iron pan over cane trash, poured into moulds, no chemicals. Growers will let you watch and will sell you a ball for a few rupees. Cutting season runs roughly December to

places.name: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary and the Thoovanam trek
places.note: A rain shadow sanctuary of dry thorn and riverine forest, which is why it looks nothing like the rest of Kerala and why it is dry enough to have no leeches. The Thoovanam waterfall trek is about 8 km return with a compulsory tribal guide, booked at the Karimutty checkpost that morning. Grizzled gian

places.name: Kanthalloor orchards
places.note: A valley that grows apples, plums, oranges, garlic and gooseberries at 1,600 metres, which nobody expects of Kerala, and smallholders will walk you round for a small fee. Fruit is on the trees roughly May to August, so outside that it is a quiet farming valley with good light and no fruit.

places.name: Vattavada vegetable villages
places.note: Terraced smallholdings at 2,000 metres growing carrots, beans, cabbage, strawberries and garlic for the Tamil Nadu markets, and the drive in from Top Station is the best hour of road in the district. Cold at dawn, genuinely cold, and the last stretch is single track with trucks on it.
places.neighborhood: Vattavada, near the Tamil Nadu border

places.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
places.note: It shuts from 12:30 to 16:00 and an itinerary that puts this after lunch loses the day. Non-Hindus are admitted through the East gate into the whole complex, including the Potramarai tank and the thousand pillar hall museum, and are stopped by signs and a guard at the two gold-roofed sanctums of Mee
places.neighborhood: Old city, inside the Masi streets

places.name: The Meenakshi night procession
places.note: Every night around 21:30 Sundareswarar is carried in a silver palanquin through the corridors to Meenakshi's bedchamber, with drums, nagaswaram and a crowd walking alongside. It is free, it takes forty minutes, and you can stand in the corridor and watch the whole thing even though you cannot enter

places.name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal
places.note: One courtyard and a dance hall of a 1636 palace that was four times this size until a later ruler carted the rest off to Tiruchirappalli. Twenty five metre columns, a domed hall with no beams, heavy Victorian restoration. Forty five minutes is plenty. The evening sound and light show on the Silappat

places.name: Puthu Mandapam
places.note: A 124-pillared Nayak hall from the 1630s with carved dynastic portraits on the columns, now occupied end to end by tailors, book stalls and tailoring machines. Nobody charges anything. A shirt made overnight costs less than the fabric does at home, and the stone is seventeenth century behind the sew
places.neighborhood: Directly east of the temple's east gopuram

places.name: Gandhi Memorial Museum
places.note: In a seventeenth century Nayak queen's palace, and it holds the blood-stained dhoti Gandhi was wearing when he was shot, which stops people dead. The rest is a long, honest and unglamorous panel history of the independence movement. Free. Hours are usually 10:00 to 13:00 and 14:00 to 17:45, but the

places.name: The Mattuthavani flower market at dawn
places.note: Madurai is the jasmine capital of India and this is where the malli comes in by the sack before dawn, gets weighed, argued over and sent to Chennai and the Gulf. Be there by 05:30. It is wet underfoot, nobody is selling to you, and the smell in a shed of a tonne of jasmine is not something you forge

places.name: Murugan Idli Shop
places.note: Started in Madurai in 1995 and now everywhere, but the Masi Street branches are the ones that matter. Idli on a banana leaf with four chutneys, sambar, and a spoon of poduthuval, refilled until you stop them. Breakfast costs about 150 rupees. Order the podi idli too.

places.name: Konar Kadai, Simmakkal
places.note: Kari dosai is a Madurai invention: minced mutton pressed into a dosa on the griddle with egg and onion, cut with a metal scraper, eaten standing. This is the stall people mean when they say it, it opens in the evening and works until after midnight, and Simmakkal at 22:00 is the busiest food corner

places.name: Amma Mess
places.note: Madurai's non-vegetarian reputation in one room: mutton chukka, kari kola urundai, brain masala, kidney, and a mutton soup drunk at the start. Nothing here is for the squeamish and nothing is subtle. Cash, plastic chairs, and the queue outside is the review.

places.name: Jigarthanda on East Marret Street
places.note: Milk boiled down, nannari sarsaparilla syrup, almond gum, ice cream, served cold in a steel tumbler and named from the Urdu for cold heart. Two shops on the same street both claim to be the original and both are good; take whichever queue is shorter. One is enough, it is very sweet, and you want it

places.name: Kanadukathan and the Athangudi tile workshops
places.note: About 1h45 each way. Merchant mansions built on Burmese teak, Italian marble and Belgian glass by a banking caste that financed half of colonial Southeast Asia, most now empty and looked after by a caretaker who will show you round for 100 to 300 rupees. The Athangudi workshops still make the colour

places.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple, the Big Temple
places.note: The sanctum shuts roughly 12:30 to 16:00, but the ASI compound stays open through the middle of the day, so unlike Meenakshi you can still walk the courtyard and the Chola frescoes corridor at noon. Finished in 1010 under Rajaraja I, a 66 metre vimana cut from granite hauled from 60 km away, and it

places.name: Thanjavur Maratha Palace and the bell tower
places.note: A half-ruined Nayak and Maratha complex where the Durbar Hall paintwork and the seven-storey Goodagopuram climb are the point, not the upkeep. Several separate ticket counters for the palace, the gallery, the library and the tower, each a few tens of rupees, each with its own attendant. Plan the gal

places.name: Thanjavur Art Gallery, the Chola bronzes
places.note: The best room of Chola bronzes anywhere, in a Nayak durbar hall with strip lighting and dusty labels, which is exactly why nobody is in it. Ninth to thirteenth century Natarajas, Parvatis and saints cast by the lost wax method that Swamimalai still uses. There is a lunch break of roughly 13:00 to 15

places.name: Saraswathi Mahal Library Museum
places.note: One of the oldest working libraries in Asia, about 49,000 palm leaf and paper manuscripts assembled by the Maratha king Serfoji II, with a small public museum of a few dozen of them plus his medical atlases and physiognomy prints. Usually closed Wednesdays, but the palace complex changes its days, s

places.name: Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram
places.note: The smallest and the best carved of the three Great Living Chola Temples, twelfth century under Rajaraja II, with a stone chariot front mandapam and a frieze of the 63 Nayanmar saints. The sanctum has a midday puja break of roughly 12:30 to 16:00 but the ASI enclosure is open through it. Free, non-H

places.name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram
places.note: Rajendra I built a capital here after marching an army to the Ganges and the temple is the only piece of that city left standing; the rest was quarried for a dam. Softer and more curved than the Thanjavur vimana, with a lion-mouthed well and a Nandi in the open. Roughly 1h45 from Thanjavur on indiff

places.name: The Swamimalai bronze foundries
places.note: Sthapathy families here still cast icons by the lost wax method the Cholas used, and the workshops will show you the beeswax model, the clay mould and the pour without any expectation that you buy. If you do buy, anything genuinely hand cast starts around 15,000 rupees and weighs what it costs to sh

places.name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam
places.note: Shut roughly 13:00 to 15:15 in the middle of the day. The largest working temple complex in the world, seven concentric walls and 21 gopurams with a 73 metre Rajagopuram finished in 1987, and the outer prakarams are a town with shops and houses inside the walls. Non-Hindus walk in freely as far as t

places.name: The Rockfort and Ucchi Pillayar Temple
places.note: 417 rock-cut steps, barefoot, up an 83 metre outcrop of some of the oldest rock on earth, with a seventh century Pallava cave temple partway and the Cauvery and Srirangam laid out at the top. Non-Hindus climb the rock and reach the summit terrace; the small Ganesha shrine at the very top is the part

places.name: Degree coffee in Kumbakonam
places.note: Degree coffee means the first, undiluted decoction off the filter, with milk that has actually been boiled, and Kumbakonam is where south India argues it is done best. It comes in a tumbler and dabara and you pour it between the two to cool it, which is not a performance, it is how you drink it. Twe

places.name: The unlimited banana leaf meals, Thanjavur
places.note: Lunch only, roughly 11:30 to 15:00, at any of the vegetarian meals hotels near the bus stand end of Gandhiji Road. A leaf, rice, four or five vegetables, sambar, rasam, kootu, buttermilk and an appalam, refilled until you fold the leaf. Around 150 rupees. Tamil meals are drier and hotter than a Kera

outings.why: Chinese nets, St Francis, the Dutch Palace murals, the synagogue and then two kilometres of open spice godowns along Bazaar Road, on foot the whole way. The hard part is the day you pick: the palace is shut Friday, the synagogue is shut Fri
outings.name: The Fort Kochi to Mattancherry walk, Bazaar Road end to end
outings.season: All year. Never on a Friday.
outings.fallback: Stop at the synagogue, take the auto back, and spend the afternoon at the Kathakali makeup instead.

outings.why: Arrive at 17:00 for the hour of face painting, stay for the hour of performance. What you are seeing is a one hour edit of a form that traditionally runs from dusk to dawn, with the story explained in English first. Real temple Kathakali ha
outings.name: Kathakali at the Kerala Kathakali Centre, from the makeup
outings.season: Nightly all year. Temple Kathakali December to April.
outings.fallback: The Kalaripayattu at 19:15 in the same hall, which is 400 rupees and better theatre than the abridged Kathakali.

outings.why: North of Kochi is the older layer: two restored synagogues of a Jewish community that predates the Portuguese, a Jewish cemetery at Chendamangalam with a 1269 tombstone, and the Cheraman Juma Masjid at Kodungallur, which claims to be the fi
outings.name: The Muziris run: Paravur synagogue, Chendamangalam and the Cheraman mosque
outings.fallback: Hill Palace Museum at Tripunithura, the largest archaeological museum in Kerala, also shut Mondays, half a day.

outings.why: A punted canoe into canals no houseboat fits down, through paddy farmed below sea level, coir retting, duck herds and toddy palms. It is the backwaters without the diesel. Go at 07:00; by 10:00 it is hot and the light is flat, and the punte
outings.name: The Kuttanad canoe out of Nedumudy
outings.season: All year. Fields are flooded June to September and green and
outings.fallback: An hour of shikara on Punnamada from the jetty, about 800 rupees, which shows you the lake and none of the villages.

outings.why: Fourteen acres of mangrove on the east shore of Vembanad, walked on raised paths at first light. November to February brings the migrants and makes it worth the early start; the rest of the year it is egrets and darters and a pleasant hour.
outings.name: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary at six thirty
outings.season: Worth it November to February; open all year
outings.fallback: Pathiramanal island by shikara, three hours, which gets you out onto the open lake instead.

outings.why: Book a slot online, drive 13 km, take the forest bus up and walk a 3 km tarred loop through shola grassland where Nilgiri tahr graze a few metres off the path. It is the single best chance in India of seeing a rare ungulate without a guide
outings.name: Rajamalai and the Eravikulam tahr
outings.season: Open all year except 1 February to 31 March
outings.fallback: The tea estate walk from Pothamedu up to the Lockhart Gap road, free, three hours, and empty.

outings.why: Out of Munnar at 04:30, swap into a 4WD at Suryanelli, an hour of rock track to a 2,100 metre ridge on the Tamil Nadu border for sunrise, then the 1930s orthodox tea factory at the top, which still runs on belt drives. The track is the hard
outings.name: The Kolukkumalai sunrise jeep
outings.season: All year, clearest December to March
outings.fallback: Top Station at 07:00 by ordinary car, one hour of driving, the same plains view from 400 metres lower.

outings.why: North over the ridge into the rain shadow: Iron Age dolmens in the fields, the state sandalwood forest, the jaggery sheds, then the Thoovanam waterfall trek in Chinnar with a compulsory tribal guide. Dry thorn forest, no leeches, and nothin
outings.name: Marayoor and Chinnar in one day
outings.season: All year. Jaggery sheds run December to April, Thoovanam is
outings.fallback: Marayoor dolmens and the jaggery sheds only, back by lunch, about four hours.

outings.why: Through the East gate before the heat, into the Potramarai tank court and the thousand pillar hall while the granite is still cool and the flower sellers are setting up. Non-Hindus go everywhere except the two gold sanctums. Phones and came
outings.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple at five thirty
outings.season: All year. Chithirai festival in April and May adds a million
outings.fallback: Puthu Mandapam and the Nayak palace, both a short walk, if the temple is shut for a procession.

outings.why: Around 21:30 every night Sundareswarar is carried in a silver palanquin to Meenakshi's bedchamber with drums and nagaswaram, and anyone standing in the corridor can watch the whole thing go past. Free, forty minutes, and almost no foreign v
outings.name: The Meenakshi night procession
outings.fallback: Kari dosai at Konar Kadai in Simmakkal, which does not get going until 21:00 anyway.

outings.why: Ninety kilometres east, about 1h45 each way, into a district of enormous merchant houses built on Burmese teak and Belgian glass and now mostly empty, opened by a caretaker for a hundred rupees. The Athangudi handmade tile workshops are the
outings.name: The Chettinad mansion loop: Kanadukathan and Athangudi
outings.season: All year. Hot and flat April to June.
outings.fallback: Azhagar Kovil and the Pazhamudircholai hill temple, 21 km north of Madurai, half a day.

outings.why: Brihadeeswarar at 06:15, when the granite is cool enough to walk barefoot and the vimana catches the first sun. Unlike Meenakshi, non-Hindus go all the way to the lingam, and the ASI compound stays open through the midday temple closure if
outings.name: The Big Temple at first light
outings.fallback: The palace art gallery and the Saraswathi Mahal library, ten minutes away, if it rains.

outings.name: Darasuram, Gangaikonda Cholapuram and the Swamimalai foundries
outings.fallback: Darasuram and Swamimalai only, five hours, skipping the northern leg.

outings.why: An hour west to the largest working temple complex on earth, seven walls deep with a town living inside them, then 417 barefoot steps up the Rockfort for the view back over it. Srirangam shuts roughly 13:00 to 15:15, the Rockfort stone is u
outings.name: Srirangam and the Rockfort
outings.fallback: Srirangam alone in the morning and back to Thanjavur for the bronzes, five hours.

destination.name: Kerala and the Tamil temple country: Kochi, Kuttanad, Munnar
destination.pitch: Twelve days buys you the best food in India, a week of water and tea hills that ask nothing of you, and then three Chola temples and a Nayak one across the ghats that are the equal of anything in the Golden Triangle with a tenth of the coac
destination.caveat: The southwest monsoon shuts the coast from June to early September and the northeast monsoon floods Tamil Nadu in October and November, so the trip really only works December to March, and even then the big temples close from about 12:30 to 16:00 every single day and most Kerala temples do not admit Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Kochi is the only real city on the route and it is a small one; Madurai is a temple with a town round it and Thanjavur is a country town with a wonder in it.
because.food: Sadya on a leaf, toddy shop fish curry with kudampuli, Mattancherry biryani that sells out by two, kari dosai at midnight in Madurai, and degree coffee in Kumbakonam, all of it under five dollars.
because.nature: Shola grassland with wild tahr at Rajamalai, a rain shadow sanctuary at Chinnar with no leeches in it, and two thousand kilometres of canal you travel by punted canoe rather than on a path.
because.culture: Meenakshi at dawn and its night procession, three Chola temples including the 1010 Big Temple, Kathakali from the makeup up, a 1568 synagogue and a church that held Vasco da Gama's body.
because.adventure: A 4WD track to Kolukkumalai at 04:30 and a guided trek to Thoovanam, and that is honestly the extent of it; this is not a trip you come to for the adrenaline.
because.relaxation: A night anchored on Vembanad, an empty fishing beach at Mararikulam, and estate mornings in Munnar where the only thing on the schedule is walking downhill through tea before breakfast.
because.exploration: Five distinct places in twelve days, none of which resembles the next: a Portuguese and Jewish port, a delta farmed below sea level, tea at two thousand metres, and a Tamil temple city that has never stopped working.
